item.title: Raidriwa emerges as pageant favourite
item.description: Miss Labasa Divisional Hospital Isabella Raidriwa has emerged as an early standout at this year’s Vodafone Festival of the Friendly North, winning two awards ahead of Saturday’s crowning. Ms Raidriwa took home the Best Research Topic and Best Sarong awards as seven contestants compete for the Miss Friendly North title.
item.content:encoded:
Miss Labasa Divisional Hospital Isabella Raidriwa has emerged as an early standout at this year’s Vodafone Festival of the Friendly North, winning two awards ahead of Saturday’s crowning.

Ms Raidriwa took home the Best Research Topic and Best Sarong awards as seven contestants compete for the Miss Friendly North title.

The Best Research Topic category was reinstated after several years, giving contestants an opportunity to demonstrate knowledge and preparation beyond traditional pageant categories.

Festival committee president Mohammed Saiyum said the move was aimed at aligning the local competition with the national Miss Fiji Pageant, which the Festival of the Friendly North currently holds.

“The committee wanted the local pageant to follow the standards of the national competition and ensure contestants understood what would be expected of them if they advanced to the Miss Fiji stage,” he said.

Mr Saiyum said judging criteria were reviewed and explained to contestants and sponsors to ensure transparency.

Meanwhile, Verenaisi Waikarawa, representing Fiji Sugar Corporation, won Best Bollywood Attire, while Selai Qarau of Galaxy and Rentals took Best Traditional Attire.

The Miss Friendly North winner will be crowned on Saturday at Subrail Park in Labasa.

item.title: Second chance for youngsters
item.description: Two-year-old Avyan Narayan and Aseri Navura, 13, will remember September 1, 2026, as their second birthday. The two were discharged from the Sri Sathya Sai Sanjeevani Heart Hospital Fiji on that day after undergoing free heart catheter procedures earlier this week.
item.content:encoded:
Two-year-old Avyan Narayan and Aseri Navura, 13, will remember September 1, 2026, as their second birthday.

The two were discharged from the Sri Sathya Sai Sanjeevani Heart Hospital Fiji on that day after undergoing free heart catheter procedures earlier this week.

Their treatment was carried out through the Sai Prema Gift of Life program during a paediatric cardiac mission led by National University Hospital Singapore, in partnership with Sanjeevani Fiji and specialist teams from Australia and India.

For the children and their families, the procedures offered more than medical treatment — they brought relief, hope and a renewed future.

Hospital director and CEO Dr Krupali Tappoo said the international collaboration demonstrated what could be achieved when specialists united for children in need.

“Our shared commitment ensures that no child is ever denied life-saving heart care due to financial circumstances,” Dr Tappoo said.

Special guest Maynesh Patel, representing Delta Company from Canada, described the initiative as generational, with today’s children benefiting from support that could shape lives for years to come.

The latest procedures add to Sanjeevani Fiji’s record of 472 successful paediatric heart surgeries, alongside 56,782 free screenings and 85,534 consultations across Fiji and the Pacific.

For Avyan and Aseri, however, the numbers are personal.

September 1 is the day their hearts were given a second chance.

item.title: BACK IN HISTORY | Chand is young accountant of the year
item.description: Back in 1993, figures fascinated Shiu Chand, whether it be at work or with community-oriented organisations. So it came as no surprise when the 30-year-old won the Young Accountant of the Year Award for the 30-35 age category.
item.content:encoded:
Back in 1993, figures fascinated Shiu Chand, whether it be at work or with community-oriented organisations.

So it came as no surprise when the 30-year-old won the Young Accountant of the Year Award for the 30-35 age category.

His prize was a $11,000 computer and software package. The award was announced at the end of a two-day conference of the Fiji Institute of Accountants at the Regent Hotel, Nadi, in 1994.

According to an article in The Fiji Times of Saturday, May 14, 1994, he began as an account audit trainee and had started immediately after finishing secondary school.

Mr Chand started working in 1981 with Vishnu Prasad & Company, a Suva-based chartered accounting firm.

He worked his way up at the company, at a number of tertiary institutions in Fiji and overseas and was promoted to the post of accounts audit intermediate.

During this time he was also involved in a correspondence course with the Trans-World Tutorial College in England aiming for a diploma in accounting, in 1983.

In 1988, he graduated from the University of the South Pacific with a bachelor’s degree in accounting.

During this time, he moved through the office ranks and was soon manager of Vishnu Prasad & Company – which is a member of the Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu, an international audit company.

In 1992, he became a partner of the firm and gained his chartered accountant certificate.

Outside of work, he served as the auditor of the Kasavu Sports and Social Club and the Sri Sath Sanatan Ram Janaki Mandali as well as a member of the Toastmasters Club.

He enjoyed tennis, soccer and swimming and was married with one son at the time the article was published.

item.title: Tribunal eyes November date for TNG appeal
item.description: THE Environmental Tribunal is aiming to hear The Next Generation Holdings (Fiji) Pte Ltd’s (TNG) appeal in November, with Magistrate Charles Ratakele saying he wants the matter completed this year. At yesterday’s Tribunal hearing TNG’s lawyer Feizal Haniff said the company had received a substantial number of supplementary documents from the Department of Environment.
item.content:encoded:
THE Environmental Tribunal is aiming to hear The Next Generation Holdings (Fiji) Pte Ltd’s (TNG) appeal in November, with Magistrate Charles Ratakele saying he wants the matter completed this year.

At yesterday’s Tribunal hearing TNG’s lawyer Feizal Haniff said the company had received a substantial number of supplementary documents from the Department of Environment.

Mr Haniff said TNG was still awaiting further documents needed to form part of the appeal record and would write to the department seeking their release.

However, the department’s lawyer, Apete Bauleka, said it would maintain its position that the documents were internal records that were not before the Director of Environment when deciding to reject TNG’s Environmental Impact Assessment report.

In response Mr Hanif said TNG would seek directions from the tribunal if the department maintained this position.

TNG appealed the Director of Environment’s June 4 decision to reject its EIA report for the proposed Vuda Point development, arguing the decision was based on errors of law and an improper exercise of statutory powers.

The matter was adjourned to September 24 for further directions.

item.title: Court jails man for life
item.description: A FIGHT over a toddy bucket on Rabi Island ended with a 25-year-old man punching another man repeatedly, resulting in his death. This led to his sentence of life imprisonment by the High Court in Labasa.
item.content:encoded:
A FIGHT over a toddy bucket on Rabi Island ended with a 25-year-old man punching another man repeatedly, resulting in his death.

This led to his sentence of life imprisonment by the High Court in Labasa.

Acting puisne Judge Penijamini Lomaloma told Birirake Bere, that he would serve a minimum term of eight years, eight months, and three weeks before a pardon may be considered.

The court heard that on October of 2024, Bere and the victim were drinking alcohol when an argument broke out.

The victim had earlier argued with his father before turning to Bere, whom he accused of hiding a bucket of toddy.

He then picked up two large stones and approached Bere, swearing before swinging at him with one of the stones.

Bere told the court he feared for his safety and punched the man who fell to the ground.

However, the court heard that Bere continued punching him for about 10 to 15 minutes until he was stopped by his aunt.

Justice Lomaloma found that Bere initially acted in self-defence, but his response became disproportionate after the victim was on the ground and no longer posed a threat.

A post mortem examination found widespread injuries to the victim’s skull and brain, with the cause of death being severe intracranial haemorrhage caused by blunt force trauma.

item.title: Police confirm body find
item.description: POLICE have confirmed the discovery of a partially decomposed body at Saweni in Lautoka yesterday morning. It is understood that Shamsad Begum who was in her 60s resided in the area.
item.content:encoded:
POLICE have confirmed the discovery of a partially decomposed body at Saweni in Lautoka yesterday morning.

It is understood that Shamsad Begum who was in her 60s resided in the area.

Her relatives had reported her missing last month.

Police spokesperson Wame Bautolu said further details would be released once investigations were completed.

A relative said her body was found behind a neighbour’s house.

Attempts to get further comments from the relative proved futile.

item.title: Fijian appointed new Air Vanuatu Airports CEO
item.description: Former Fiji Airways executive Shalendra Maharaj has been appointed the new Chief Executive Officer of Airports Vanuatu Limited (AVL). Maharaj, who previously served as Executive Manager Operations at Fiji Airways, will take up the five-year appointment on October 1, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
Former Fiji Airways executive Shalendra Maharaj has been appointed the new Chief Executive Officer of Airports Vanuatu Limited (AVL).

Maharaj, who previously served as Executive Manager Operations at Fiji Airways, will take up the five-year appointment on October 1, 2026.

His appointment follows a competitive recruitment process that attracted candidates from Vanuatu, the Pacific and internationally.

Maharaj is currently Manager Aviation Services at Newman, Marble Bar and Nullagine airports in Australia, overseeing airport operations, safety, security, regulatory compliance and performance.

His aviation career includes senior roles with Fiji Airways, Emirates, Qantas Airways, dnata and Pionair Australia.

At Fiji Airways, Maharaj provided strategic leadership across flight scheduling, ground operations, maintenance and logistics.

The AVL Board said his extensive airline and airport experience, together with expertise in infrastructure redevelopment, risk management and regulatory compliance, makes him well suited to lead the organisation.

He succeeds Jason Rakau, who has served as AVL chief executive since 2016.

AVL Board chairman Jesse Benjamin said Maharaj’s leadership comes at an important time for Vanuatu’s aviation sector, with the country’s airports playing a critical role in tourism, trade, investment and national connectivity.

item.title: Call for serious climate talks
item.description: WITH less than a month before Fiji hosts the Pre-COP30 in Nadi, communities in Vanua Levu are calling for climate discussions to translate into practical support for those already facing its impact. Headman of Naviavia settlement in Macuata, Marika Sade, said flooding and rising seawater had affected the community’s crops, river resources, and income for about 10 years.
item.content:encoded:
WITH less than a month before Fiji hosts the Pre-COP30 in Nadi, communities in Vanua Levu are calling for climate discussions to translate into practical support for those already facing its impact.

Headman of Naviavia settlement in Macuata, Marika Sade, said flooding and rising seawater had affected the community’s crops, river resources, and income for about 10 years.

The settlement is home to about 245 descendants of Solomon Islanders whose ancestors came to Fiji during the blackbirding era.

Mr Sade said one of the biggest concerns for the community was the declining size of crops, particularly dalo.

“Previously, our dalo grew well and was of good quality, but now it is not the same. Before, the dalo used to grow much bigger. Now, the size is smaller,” he said.

This has affected families who depend on farming for their income.

“The floods had also washed away parts of the riverbank and damaged crops, while seawater had intruded parts of the area.”

He said changes were also being noticed in the river, with fish and other resources declining in numbers.

“We can still find fish now, but not like before,” he said.

He said fisher folks now travel further out to sea to catch fish.

“Practical support would help communities protect the resources they depend on and better prepare for growing climate pressures.”
